the-jefferson.what: Arthur Weinstein's illegal after-hours club in the old Jefferson Theatre on 14th Street - the first of his after-hours clubs, before the Continental and The World (1984).
the-jefferson.address: Jefferson Theatre, 214 East 14th Street near Third Avenue (auditorium ran through to East 13th Street). The club was upstairs: the second floor above the marquee.
the-jefferson.years: Opened c. New Year's 1981 (a 1980 party Weinstein threw for his wife Colleen in their loft there turned into the club the same night, per the Daily Beast; Scotty Taylor dates the opening to New Year's 1981). Closed by c. 1982-83 (Arthur was already building the Continental in a garage on West 25th Street). Exact closing date not found.
the-jefferson.who: Arthur Weinstein (died 2008), with his wife Colleen Weinstein; Scotty Taylor says he was a partner. Building owner Semone Grossman had backed out of a plan to turn the whole theatre into a club.
the-jefferson.the_building: Opened 1913 as B.F. Keith's Jefferson vaudeville theatre (architects George W. Keister, Thomas W. Lamb), later RKO Jefferson; showed films until at least 1977, then stood empty; demolished 2000; now CityMD (14th St) and apartments (13th St).
the-jefferson.guests_say: Susanne Bartsch went there in her first weeks in New York, 1981 - 'the one place in New York that felt fabulous' (James, S02E03). Eric Goode: Arthur 'brought down the Ninth and Tenth Precinct' wearing a wire (S03E06).
the-jefferson.picture: Drawn for the AFTERPARTY (Gemini): header (a night upstairs in the faded theatre, c. 1981) and polaroid (the marquee on East 14th Street) in clubs/jefferson/. No free photo of the building exists.
sources: NYT obituary 'Arthur Weinstein, Starter of Nightclubs, Dies at 60', 16 Jul 2008

nations.what: 'Nations' - Chi Chi Valenti's essay on the downtown 'tribes in the night that hung together like families, like style tribes': the House of Xtravaganza, Patricia Field and the House of Field, Keith Haring and his staff ('the Haringtons'), and the Pyramid Club. Photos by Timothy Greenfield-Sanders.
nations.issue: DETAILS, Vol. 7 No. 5, October 1988 (222 pages). Same issue: William Coupon's 'The Mudd Pack' (the Mudd Club at 10), Stephen Saban's column with Patrick McMullan photos, Marcus Leatherdale's Hidden Identities, Chuck D by Steven Blush.
nations.cover_star: Tina L'Hotsky, photographed by William Coupon. Cover lines: 'Fashionation', 'Mudd Club 1978, Club Houses 1988'.
spreads: covers/nations/details-1988-10-nations-haringtons.jpg (Keith Haring and the Haringtons, for Nations)
nations.check: Chi Chi says she picked four tribes, one being the House of Xtravaganza; Gallery 98's listing names Patricia Field, Keith Haring and the Pyramid. Latina.com captions an Xtravaganza group photo (David DePino, Danni, Mother Angie, Jose Disla) 'Details, October 1988'.

the-death-of-downtown.what: 'The Death of Downtown' - Michael Musto's Village Voice cover story, written after Andy Warhol died (22 Feb 1987).
the-death-of-downtown.publication: The Village Voice, 1987 (cover story). Exact issue date not found online - the Voice archive or a library database would have it.
the-death-of-downtown.argued: With Warhol, 'the centerpiece of the scene', gone, the clubs and the excitement were dying: yuppies and 'the dreaded bridge-and-tunnel people' were taking over, the press was drying up, the grown-up 'clink clink' party at Area's VIP room was past. It ended: 'nothing's ever really over, something's going to come back to kick everyone in the pants - it might be a revolution' (Musto, S01E02). James: the vacuum was filled by Michael Alig and the club kids (S06E01).
the-death-of-downtown.related: Musto's book 'Downtown' (Vintage, 12 Jun 1986, ISBN 0-394-74285-0) - with the Warhol blurb Musto says he wrote himself (S01E02 00:30:23). His later Voice piece 'Wild in the Clubs' (1988) is a different article.

howie-pyro.who: Howie Pyro (Howard Kusten, 28 Jun 1960 - 4 May 2022). Teen leader of The Blessed at CBGB and Max's; early Mudd Club DJ; first DJ at Squeezebox (Michael Schmidt, S02E06); co-founder and bassist of D Generation; bassist in Danzig 2000-2003; DJ and host of Intoxica Radio (internet radio: 1950s-60s rock'n'roll, garage, surf, rockabilly); 'Howie Pyro's Sick Sick World' (Grease Rhythm TV). Died of COVID-19 pneumonia complications after a liver transplant.
